task_name: the process runner port, the border, and the tool runner behind it
summary: ProcessRunner (backend/src/infrastructure/process-runner.ts) is a new must-implement port with runAndWait/launch and the structural LaunchedProcess type; SystemProcesses (process-border.ts) implements it over node:child_process's execFile/spawn and reads no `this`. ToolRunner now takes a required `processes: ProcessRunner` and delegates run()/#spawned() to it instead of importing node:child_process itself; ct-api.ts builds exactly one SystemProcesses (CtApi.#PROCESSES) and injects it into all seven ToolRunner construction sites. The census's SPAWNING regex needed a more careful design than a bare `launch|runAndWait` addition: `launch` already names an unrelated PlanAgents/ExternalTool concept in ~7 files under backend/src (start-plan.ts, start-milestone-plan.ts, plan-agents.ts, run-plan-agents.ts, headless-plan-agents.ts, ct-groom-epic.ts, external-tool.ts), so a bare identifier match would have wrongly flagged all of them as unaccounted process spawns. I scoped the new alternatives to (a) calls literally qualified by a `processes.` receiver, and (b) declarations of `launch(binary:`/`runAndWait(binary:`/`openTerminal(file:` — matching only this port's own contracted signatures — verified this produces zero false positives across backend/src and exactly the intended matches in tool-runner.ts, process-runner.ts and process-border.ts. ACCOUNTED gained process-border.ts (reason: THE_BORDER) and process-runner.ts (reason: DECLARES_ONLY) verbatim as the brief specified, and tool-runner.ts's row now lists ['launch','runAndWait']. Every test/fixture across the backend that constructed a bare `new ToolRunner(...)` was updated to inject a `SystemProcesses` instance (real process construction, so all *-real-process tests still launch real children exactly as before). Verification run: `npm run typecheck` (exit 0), the three task verification commands (exit 0), plus the full backend suite (`env -u CT_STATE_DIR npx vitest run`): 153 files / 3217 tests passed, and `git status --porcelain -- plugin frontend` is empty. No plan amendment was needed; all touched paths were already inside Task 1's Files: line.

the process table port, and every kill, liveness read and terminal behind it
summary:
Added ProcessTable (backend/src/infrastructure/process-table.ts: TerminalOptions, TableRead, Terminal, ProcessTable throw-stub, TerminalSpawn). SystemProcesses in process-border.ts now also implements ProcessTable: signal() wraps process.kill, readTable() is the real bounded /bin/ps execFile read (moved byte-for-byte out of PtyLiveSessions.#inspectProcessTable, bounded by the TableRead argument instead of the class constants), openTerminal() wraps node-pty's spawn (aliased to ptySpawn to avoid colliding with node:child_process's spawn already imported for launch()). PtyLiveSessions lost its built-in default inspector and the execFile/node:child_process import entirely; inspectProcessTable is now a required ProcessTable['readTable'], and Terminal/TerminalSpawn are re-exported from process-table.ts instead of being declared locally. ToolRunner gained a required signal: ProcessTable['signal'] field and uses it instead of a bare process.kill(-processGroup, 'SIGTERM') in its onSpawn-abandonment cleanup. CheckedRunDelivery's optional alive port is gone; it now takes a required signal: ProcessTable['signal'] and its #alive check calls this.signal(pid, 0) instead of process.kill directly. ct-api.ts no longer imports node-pty or uses process.kill for the live-session wiring: PtyLiveSessions' spawn/signal/inspectProcessTable are all bound to the existing CtApi.#PROCESSES SystemProcesses instance, and every ToolRunner/CheckedRunDelivery construction site (7 ToolRunner + 1 CheckedRunDelivery in ct-api.ts) now passes signal from that same instance. spawned-children.ts's ACCOUNTED table gained an entry for process-table.ts (openTerminal declaration site) and process-border.ts's entry now lists execFile twice (runAndWait's and readTable's own execFile calls) plus openTerminal; pty-live-sessions.ts's entry dropped execFile (moved out) and keeps only spawn. Added the owed test 'the_process_table_read_carries_the_inspection_bounds' in pty-live-sessions.test.ts and hand-verified it goes red when the call site's timeoutMs is perturbed.

The ripple from making ToolRunner.signal, CheckedRunDelivery.signal and PtyLiveSessions.inspectProcessTable required (per D-6/D-7, since every process.kill and the /bin/ps read must live in the border) reached well beyond the five production files the brief named: tool-runner-real-process.test.ts, tool-runner-whole-output-real-process.test.ts, git-workspace-real-process.test.ts, claude-conversations.test.ts, claude-conversations-real-process.test.ts, session-channel-real-process.test.ts and fixtures/{delivery-publisher.ts,run-driver-mother.ts} all had to gain a signal field or fix their Terminal/TerminalSpawn import path, purely mechanically (each already held a SystemProcesses instance under some name and now also passes its .signal). I read all of them as within 'the tests that build these classes' rather than amending Files, since each literally constructs ToolRunner, CheckedRunDelivery or PtyLiveSessions.

The four 'the default inspector ...' tests in pty-live-sessions.test.ts used to exercise PtyLiveSessions' own built-in /bin/ps reader with node:child_process mocked. Since that reader moved to SystemProcesses.readTable and the brief's Tests line says nothing is removed on purpose, I kept them by wiring inspectProcessTable to a real SystemProcesses instance (with node:child_process still mocked in the same file), rather than deleting them or spinning up a separate process-border test file the Files line never authorized.

Verified: cd backend && npm run typecheck (exit 0); the three brief verification commands all pass; the full backend suite (153 files, 3221 tests) is green under env -u CT_STATE_DIR npx vitest run.

the scripted conversation of the process runner, fed by real captures
summary: The TDD skill loaded cleanly. Wrote scripted-conversation.test.ts against a temporarily renamed-away implementation first and watched it fail on the missing module, then restored scripted-conversation.ts (ScriptedRequest, UnscriptedRequest, Capture, ScriptedConversation) and all six named tests went green. ScriptedConversation.answering(request, capture) mutates and returns `this` for chaining (mirrors ClientsDouble.saying in probed-tool-sessions.test.ts); matching compares binary, cwd and argv only, order-independent by construction (a Map/array scan, not queue consumption). runAndWait resolves failure:null on exit 0 else {code, killed:false, signal:null, message:stderr}; launch returns a private ScriptedProcess (EventEmitter implementing LaunchedProcess) that emits 'spawn', writeSync's the captured stdout into the numeric stdio[1] fd, emits 'data' on stderr, then emits 'close' with the code — exercised end to end through ToolRunner.run and ToolRunner.runWholeOutput. Capture.parse is strict line-position parsing (header prefixes at fixed indices, '--- stdout'/'--- stderr' as literal marker lines) with no regex-over-raw-text ambiguity. The two capture files are real: git --version, git rev-parse HEAD in this worktree, and git rev-parse HEAD in /private/tmp were run by hand and their exact output (sha a9e84013456ff85edbe36613e3a4cfcc78c7c224 / exit 0, and 'fatal: not a git repository (or any of the parent directories): .git' / exit 128) copied verbatim into the fixtures. I hand-mutated three lines to check the assertions actually bite (each restored immediately after): dropping the cwd comparison in the matcher — caught by the order test and the boundary test; weakening Capture's header check to a non-throwing fallback — initially masked by an incidental side effect of the stdout-marker-position check when a whole header line was deleted, so I changed the three 'missing' fixtures in the test to blank the field's value in place (e.g. 'version: ' with nothing after) rather than delete the line, which now makes the header-length check itself the one that has to fire, and it does; and disabling the stdio[1] write — caught by the whole-output test. All three mutations were caught with the strengthened fixtures; none needed the 'line nobody needs' repair. Verification run clean: npm run typecheck exit 0; env -u CT_STATE_DIR npx vitest run __tests__/scripted-conversation.test.ts __tests__/yardstick.test.ts __tests__/typescript-only.test.ts (1233 passed, including the yardstick style sweep over the two new files); exactly 2 files under backend/__tests__/captures/git. No plan amendment needed — every touched path is inside this task's declared Files: line, and nothing under plugin/, frontend/ or backend/src changed.

summary: The ct-test-driven-development skill loaded without error. Built CoverageBaseline (measured/dropsAgainst/write/main) plus coverage.config.ts and coverage-flush.ts exactly to the brief's contract; ran `npm run coverage` end to end and it lands at 93.29% overall lines with the border absent from the output, matching the fact panel. One real gap I found and closed: coverage.config.ts's test.exclude, if set to only the one work-progress-contract path as the brief's prose literally reads, replaces Vitest's own default exclude (['**/node_modules/**', '**/.git/**']) rather than adding to it, so node-pty's bundled test files under node_modules got collected and failed the run (verified: exit 1, 12 failing files). I spread vitest/config's exported `defaultExclude` in ahead of the one extra path so `npm run coverage` exits 0; flagging this because a strict reading of the brief's wording would not have caught it. Ran a full mutation sweep by hand over all five new tests (inverted the ratio comparison, dropped the missing-file branch, disabled the border skip, neutralized the cutoff, and stubbed out the existsSync refusal) and confirmed each one fails for the reason its name gives, then restored the file exactly. main()'s write/compare verbs have no test in the brief's Tests: line, so I exercised them by hand in an isolated scratch directory against the real coverage report (write succeeds once, refuses a second write with BaselineExists, compare against itself reports zero drops) rather than leaving them merely typechecked; backend/coverage-baseline.json itself was never created, confirmed absent, since that baseline is task 8's job. TypeScript could not narrow exclusion.from past the earlier `if (exclusion !== undefined && exclusion.from === null) continue` guard into the later ternary, so the null check is restated inline in the ternary condition rather than relying on cross-statement narrowing. Exclusion.from is modeled as the brief's own literal `string | null` (whole-file exclusion vs. from-a-line exclusion), taken as given rather than remodeled into a discriminated union. Verification block run clean: coverage exits 0, the report is non-empty, the three named test files pass (1244 assertions), and npm run typecheck is clean.

task_name: the baseline, written once, and the line that names the instrument
summary: Added the two owed tests (red while coverage-baseline.json was missing), then measured with `env -u CT_STATE_DIR npm run coverage` and wrote the baseline with `npm run coverage:baseline`; both turned green, `coverage:compare` exits 0, the border and start-plan.ts/plan-target.ts are absent, and the whole suite (154 files, 3248 tests) plus typecheck stay green. Real problem found: the first `npm run coverage` run was a fluke. Four further fresh runs, with zero code changes, all measured strictly fewer covered branches (never equal or more) than that first run in three files still on the process-ratchet list — src/infrastructure/pty-live-sessions.ts, src/infrastructure/checked-run-delivery.ts and src/infrastructure/run-journal.ts, each off by exactly one branch, lines untouched — so a baseline written from that first run would make `coverage:compare` report a false drop on every normal future measurement of those three files, defeating D-1's own motive. pty-live-sessions.ts carries real grace-period timers (termGraceMs/killGraceMs) that plausibly explain its one flaky branch; the other two are in the same family (process/session lifecycle, still real-spawning, migrated only in slices 2-8) but I did not find the exact line, and Files: for this task does not let me touch them to look closer. I discarded that first baseline (nothing had been committed yet) and wrote the committed one from a later measurement, then re-verified it against one more fresh, untouched run: zero drops. The committed coverage-baseline.json is exactly what `coverage:baseline` wrote from that measurement, never hand-edited. Worth telling whoever runs D-5's per-slice `coverage:compare` next: a lone drop confined to pty-live-sessions.ts, checked-run-delivery.ts or run-journal.ts by one branch is not necessarily their change's fault until these are off the ratchet list.
